topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: CI ratchet — scheduled upstream-geth build with a tightening baseline
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257.

## Goal

Make decoupling progress measurable and regression-proof: a scheduled CI job that continuously
rehearses the #20266 cutover, so the final flip is a formality instead of a leap of faith.

## Design

- Script (also runnable locally): in a throwaway checkout, drop the go.mod `replace` for
  go-ethereum, pin the upstream version matching the current op-geth base, `go mod tidy`,
  then `go build`/`go vet` the tree and emit the list of packages that fail.
- Compare against a **committed baseline** file of known-failing packages:
  - a package failing that is *not* in the baseline → job fails (regression: someone reintroduced
    a fork-API use into a clean package);
  - a baselined package now building clean → job asks to remove it from the baseline (ratchet
    tightens; only ever shrinks).
- Scheduled daily (per current CI conventions for scheduled tests), plus manually triggerable.
- Cutover (#20266) = baseline reaches empty; the flip PR deletes the job and the baseline.

Notes: the differential tests in op-core are expected baseline members until cutover (they import
op-geth-only symbols by design). Go reports only frontier packages — the baseline compares
*failing package sets*, not error counts, which is stable under that behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scheduled job green on the current baseline; a seeded fork-API regression in a clean package
  turns it red.
- Baseline file + one-command local reproduction documented in the decoupling doc.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: delete op-chain-ops/cmd/receipt-reference-builder
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Delete [`op-chain-ops/cmd/receipt-reference-builder`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/a3724b8d6a5e52a21f743ea5e3fe7f5b43384948/op-chain-ops/cmd/receipt-reference-builder). It collects receipt data for chains with post-Bedrock, pre-Canyon activity, and nothing uses it today. It is also one of the remaining op-geth-only API users: it reads the fork's `Transaction.EffectiveNonce`. Deleting it removes that use instead of porting it, like the pre-Holocene `check-*` tools (#21746).

Includes the references outside the code (docs, build and CI config) and its entry in the `opgeth-ratchet` allowlist.

topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock,op-devstack: follow-up nits from the SuperchainETHBridge refund review
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #23284 (`contracts-bedrock!: refund expired SuperchainETHBridge sends`). These are the non-blocking review nits from that PR, deferred so its approvals stand. None of them changes contract behavior.

**Contract tests**

- [ ] **Make the `sendETH`-from-messenger test cover the guard** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533304)). The test sends to destination `901`, the test chain's own `block.chainid`, so the relay already reverts with `MessageDestinationSameChain` without the `SuperchainETHBridge_SenderIsMessenger` guard. Use `902`, so that without the guard the relay would succeed. The balance asserts after the expected revert can never fail; drop or restructure them.
- [ ] **Test the hazardous zero-period case** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533327)). `test_expireMessage_uninitializedPeriod_reverts` uses word dated `type(uint64).max`. Also check word dated `sentAt + 1` reverts with `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger_InvalidExpiryPeriod` while the period is unset, since that is the case the guard exists for.

**Acceptance tests and DSL**

- [ ] **Move the refund's receipt arithmetic into the DSL** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533352)). The fee sum in `messageexpiry_test.go` leaves out the operator fee and panics if `L1Fee` is nil. Add a DSL action such as `func (s *ETHSend) Refund(user *EOA) eth.ETH` that sends the call, requires a successful receipt (not asserted today; `contract.Write` only checks inclusion), and returns the gas cost through the shared helper in `op-devstack/dsl/bridge.go`.
- [ ] **Check `Refunded()` is false before the refund** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533363)), and after the rejected refund in `TestUnrelayedMessageCannotExpireBeforeExpiryPeriod`.
- [ ] **Use `eth.ETH` for the binding's amount** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533372)) in `op-service/txintent/bindings/SuperchainETHBridge.go`, like the other bindings, so the DSL can pass `s.amount` directly.
- [ ] **Build one `SuperchainETHBridge` binding in the DSL** ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533381)) with `WithClient`/`WithTest` at the send site, instead of a second one in `op-devstack/dsl/superchain_eth_bridge.go`.

**Not carried over**

- The `L2ContractsManager` 1.16.0 → 1.16.1 patch bump in #23284 changes only the version string ([comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23284#discussion_r4275533315)). The versioning policy asks for no bump in that case, but once #23284 merges the version is already on develop, so there is nothing to undo.

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona-node!: build derived payloads at forkchoiceUpdated
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Alternative: #23454 builds derived payloads in a payload service wrapper instead, with no reth changes.

op-reth only found out that a derived block's transactions were invalid in its asynchronous payload build, after `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` had already answered VALID. An invalid forced transaction was skipped, so op-reth built a block that the fault proof rejects. An invalid `0x7D` failed the build instead, so `engine_getPayload` returned an error, the rollup node retried the same attributes forever and the safe head stalled.

op-reth now builds the payload of `noTxPool` attributes that carry a non-deposit transaction exactly once inside `engine_forkchoiceUpdated`. It does so in `OpEngineApi` with op-reth's payload builder, whatever payload service the node runs, so op-reth-premium is covered too, and answers `-38003` when the transactions make the block invalid. op-node and kona-node (fixed here) then replace the block with a deposits-only one. Deposit-only `noTxPool` attributes still go to the payload service.

- `engine_getPayload` hands the executed block to the engine tree through a new reth hook, `PayloadBuilderHandle::publish_built_payload` (ethereum-optimism/reth#16), so `engine_newPayload` doesn't execute it a second time.
- Attributes reth rejects keep reth's exact response. A build that fails for a node-local reason (missing state, provider error, panic) is never `-38003`; it takes the payload-service path as before.
- A retried request joins the running build or gets the built payload, and forkchoice updates are handled one at a time, so a fallback can't overwrite a newer forkchoice.
- For derived attributes with an invalid transaction, `debug_executePayload` returns the witness up to that transaction, where the fault proof program stops, instead of the witness of a block without it.

Latency for 30M-gas blocks (release build, median of 9, FCU + getPayload + newPayload + FCU), before → after: ETH transfers 120 → 95 ms, SSTORE 14 → 24 ms, KECCAK256 165 → 159 ms, ecrecover 388 → 389 ms, all within run-to-run noise (±10–20 ms). An invalid block is rejected at FCU after executing up to the failing transaction.

Supersedes #23188, whose kona-node fix and acceptance test this carries. Compared with it and with an earlier private fix (optimism-private@ed9e4d8):

| | #23188 | ed9e4d8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where it checks | payload job generator, at job creation | `OpEngineValidator::validate_payload_attributes_against_header` | `OpEngineApi`, in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` |
| Derived attributes covered | `0x7D` only | all with a non-deposit tx | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) |
| Executions per derived block | 1 | 2 (validate, then build) | 1 |
| op-reth-premium | not covered (own job generator) | covered | covered |
| Invalid forced tx skipped (fault-proof mismatch) | yes | fixed | fixed |
| kona-node fix + acceptance test | yes | no | yes |
| Upstream changes | none | none | reth hook (ethereum-optimism/reth#16) |
| Costs | blocks the payload service while building; copy of reth's payload service builder | double execution; breaking `Evm` parameter on `OpEngineValidator` | copies reth's attribute checks; FCU serialized by a lock |

**Before merge:** move the reth pin from the head of ethereum-optimism/reth#16 to its commit on `optimism`, and re-tag the stale `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` reth tags (`just mirrors stale`); the only reth change is the payload-service hook.

Review agents (Rust, Go, derivation-batch, security) ran; their findings are fixed except:
- Dismissed, to confirm: no timeout on a derived build that holds the forkchoice lock. Builds are bounded by the block gas limit, a stuck state provider stalls reth's engine tree as well, and a request the rollup node abandons releases the lock.
- Not changed here, as kona-node with op-geth already behaves so: before Holocene, kona-node retries a `-38003` for derived attributes instead of dropping them; kona-node and kona-client gate the deposits-only replacement on the L2 timestamp, op-node on the L1 origin's; a transient error while building the replacement is critical.

BREAKING CHANGE: op-reth answers `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` with `-38003` when the transactions of derived attributes make the block invalid. op-node handles this. kona-node needs the change in this PR, otherwise it retries and stalls the safe head, so upgrade both together. Rust callers of `OpEngineApi::new` must pass the provider, validator and `DerivedPayloads` it builds derived payloads with, and `OpEngineApiBuilder` requires the node's pool, provider and EVM to fit op-reth's payload builder.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona-node!: build derived payloads in a payload service wrapper
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Alternative to #23447: same fix, built in a payload service wrapper instead of `OpEngineApi`, with no reth changes.

op-reth only found out that a derived block's transactions were invalid in its asynchronous payload build, after `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` had already answered VALID. An invalid forced transaction was skipped, so op-reth built a block that the fault proof rejects. An invalid `0x7D` failed the build instead, so `engine_getPayload` returned an error, the rollup node retried the same attributes forever and the safe head stalled.

`DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder` wraps a payload service builder. For `noTxPool` attributes that carry a non-deposit transaction, the service it spawns builds the payload exactly once, with op-reth's payload builder and the engine tree's resources, before it answers the engine's `BuildNewPayload` command. The engine awaits that answer in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` and turns a failure into `-38003`, so op-node and kona-node (fixed here) replace the block with a deposits-only one. Every other command goes to the wrapped service. `OpNode` wraps its payload service; op-reth-premium opts in with a one-line wrap.

- The build runs on a blocking task. The engine tree doesn't wait for it; only the forkchoiceUpdated response does.
- `engine_getPayload` resolves the built payload like a payload job's and emits `Events::BuiltPayload` on the first resolution, as reth's service does, so `engine_newPayload` doesn't execute the block a second time.
- A build that fails for a node-local reason (missing state, provider error, panic) is never `-38003`; it goes to the wrapped service with the engine's leases. If that fails too, `engine_getPayload` fails and the rollup node retries.
- A retried request joins the running build or gets the built payload.
- For derived attributes with an invalid transaction, `debug_executePayload` returns the witness up to that transaction, where the fault proof program stops, instead of the witness of a block without it.

Supersedes #23188, whose kona-node fix and acceptance test this carries. Compared with it, with an earlier private fix (optimism-private@ed9e4d8) and with #23447:

| | #23188 | ed9e4d8 | #23447 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where it checks | payload job generator, at job creation | `OpEngineValidator::validate_payload_attributes_against_header` | `OpEngineApi`, in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` | payload service wrapper, at `BuildNewPayload` |
| Derived attributes covered | `0x7D` only | all with a non-deposit tx | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) |
| Executions per derived block | 1 | 2 (validate, then build) | 1 | 1 |
| op-reth-premium | not covered (own job generator) | covered | covered | covered with a one-line wrap |
| Invalid forced tx skipped (fault-proof mismatch) | yes | fixed | fixed | fixed |
| kona-node fix + acceptance test | yes | no | yes | yes |
| Upstream changes | none | none | reth hook (ethereum-optimism/reth#16) | none |
| Costs | blocks the payload service while building; copy of reth's payload service builder | double execution; breaking `Evm` parameter on `OpEngineValidator` | copies reth's attribute checks; FCU serialized by a lock | payload services must opt in |

Downsides of this approach:
- A payload service that isn't wrapped isn't covered: premium and third-party node builders must opt in.
- It proxies reth's `PayloadServiceCommand` enum; a new command upstream needs a match arm here (a compile error, not a silent gap).
- `Events::BuiltPayload` must fire exactly when reth's service fires it, or `engine_newPayload` re-executes the block.
- `-38003` carries no reason; it is only in op-reth's logs.
- After a node-local failure, the wrapped service's fallback build runs without the tree's execution cache and state root task (it keeps the leases).

Review agents (Rust, security) ran; their findings are fixed except, to confirm:
- The switch to all `noTxPool` attributes stays a `const`, as that choice is still open.
- A payload id collision with different attributes is only partly handled: a request joins a build or a built payload only if the attributes match too, but `engine_getPayload` looks payloads up by id. Ids hash every attribute field, and reth trusts them the same way.
- `Events::Attributes` is emitted when a derived build starts, as reth does when it creates a job, so after a node-local failure the wrapped service emits it again. Nothing in reth consumes it.
- After the shutdown signal, a forkchoiceUpdated with attributes gets `-38003`, as with reth's own payload service.
- Not changed here, as in #23447: a transient error while kona-node builds the deposits-only replacement is critical, and kona-node gates the replacement on the L2 timestamp, op-node on the L1 origin's.

The kona-node and acceptance-test commits are the ones from #23447, where the Go and derivation-batch reviewers ran.

BREAKING CHANGE: op-reth answers `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` with `-38003` when the transactions of derived attributes make the block invalid. op-node handles this. kona-node needs the change in this PR, otherwise it retries and stalls the safe head, so upgrade both together. `OpNodeComponentBuilder`'s default payload service builder is now `DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder<OpPayloadServiceBuilder>`; nodes that replace the payload service must wrap theirs in `DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder` to be covered.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: Per-chain Review Period
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
Closes [#686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/686)

## Description

Makes the withdrawal review period configurable per chain. `PROOF_MATURITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (OptimismPortal2) and `DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (AnchorStateRegistry) move from constructor immutables on the shared implementations to per-chain proxy storage, set at `initialize()` and changeable through an L1PAO-only setter. The implementations keep a min/max pair of constructor immutables that bound every write.

OPCM carries each chain's live value forward on upgrade. The Migrator preserves each portal's and legacy registry's value and gives the shared AnchorStateRegistry the value the legacy registries agree on. op-deployer takes the delays as per-chain inputs and the bounds as implementation inputs.

Of the ~2,000 lines added, 786 are Solidity tests, 183 are regenerated snapshots, and most of the 576 Go lines are gofmt realignment of struct literals that gained the longer bound field names. The reviewable contract change is ~460 lines.

## Design decisions

- Storage, not immutables: `proofMaturityDelaySeconds` lands in portal slot 64 and `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` in registry slot 7, both tagged `@custom:network-specific`. The existing getters keep their selectors, so every reader of the delays is unaffected.

- `initialize()` and the setter share one internal `_set…` that bounds-checks, stores and emits the `…Set` event, following `SystemConfig._setGasLimit`.

- Bounds are constructor immutables with getters, standard `[1 d, 7 d]` for proof maturity and `[12 h, 3.5 d]` for the finality delay. The constructor and `DeployImplementations` reject `min == 0` and `min > max`; there is no chain-id floor in the deploy script, since VerifyOPCM checks the bound immutables at release and the StandardValidator pins the implementation.

- No `upgrade` override for the delays due to the contract size limit on the OPCM. `_loadFullConfig` reads the live getters and passes them back to `initialize()`; `overrides.cfg.proofMaturityDelaySeconds` / `…disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` are not allow-listed and are rejected as unknown instructions. The setters are the only write path after deployment; For atomic upgrade and delay setting batch the calls in the same superchain-ops batch.

- Due to the contract size limit, OPCM does not validate the delays and the values are checked directly on the implementation.

- It is assumed that on the time of interop migration, chains will share the same delays. The shared ASR is initialized with the finality delay every chain's registry reports, or `migrate()` reverts with `OPContractsManagerMigrator_DisputeGameFinalityDelayMismatch` before any portal is touched. The shared-registry `initialize` moved into `_initializeSharedAnchorStateRegistry` because evaluating the agreement check inline in `migrate()` hits stack-too-deep.

- `StandardValidator` gains range checks (`PORTAL-100`, `…-ANCHORP-80`): "standard" now means within the sanctioned range. `VerifyOPCM` verifies the bound immutables on the implementations (`EXPECTED_MIN_/MAX_…` env vars with standard defaults) instead of a delay value the implementation no longer holds.

- op-deployer: the delays move from `SuperchainProofParams` to `ChainProofParams` under the same JSON keys, so existing `globalDeployOverrides` keep working and per-chain `deployOverrides` can differ; the bounds take their place as implementation inputs. `op-devstack` and `op-e2e` widen the bounds for their short devnet delays.

- Versions: OptimismPortal2 6.0.0, AnchorStateRegistry 5.0.0 (constructor and `initialize` ABI change, reinit versions bumped), OPContractsManagerStandardValidator 4.1.0, OPCM V2 9.0.3 (lands in the in-development 9.x release).

## Tests

Contracts, from `packages/contracts-bedrock`:

- `just pr` — build, lint, snapshots, semver-lock, interfaces, spacers, semgrep, size check.
- `just test-dev --match-contract 'OptimismPortal2_|AnchorStateRegistry_|OPContractsManagerV2_Deploy_Test|OPContractsManagerStandardValidator_|DeployImplementations_|DeployOPChain_|VerifyOPCM_|Initializable_|SetDisputeGameImpl'` — setter and `initialize` matrix (access control, bounds, events), delay changes applied to already-proven withdrawals and already-resolved games, deploy stores the delays in proxy storage, bounds errors on deploy, rejected override keys, StandardValidator range codes, VerifyOPCM bound checks.
- `DEV_FEATURE__OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP=true just test-dev --match-contract OPContractsManagerV2_Migrate_Test` — portal and legacy-registry delays preserved, shared registry inherits the agreed value, mismatch reverts.
- `just test-dev --match-path test/invariants/OptimismPortal2.t.sol` — the ProxyAdmin owner is excluded as a sender so the fuzzer cannot move the window under the invariants.
- `just test-upgrade` (needs `ETH_RPC_URL`) — `test_upgrade_withdrawalDelaysUnchangedWithoutOverride_succeeds` proves the 7 d / 3.5 d carry-forward through the real upgrade path.

Go, from the repo root:

- `just lint-go` passes.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/bootstrap/ ./op-chain-ops/interopgen/...` — struct mirrors load against the current script ABIs on both the script-host and forge paths, `ResolveChainProofParams` defaults and per-chain overrides, bootstrap `Check()` bound cases.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/integration_test/ -run TestProofParamOverrides` — bounds verified as implementation immutables, delays verified in portal slot 64 and registry slot 7 of the deployed proxies.

## Additional context

`op-deployer bootstrap implementations` replaces `--proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` with `--min-/--max-proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--min-/--max-dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` (env `…_MIN_/MAX_…`). Operators who set the delays through `globalDeployOverrides` are unaffected; the keys now configure the chain rather than the implementation. Chains whose live delay is outside the bounds cannot upgrade until they redeploy; every production chain is at 7 d / 3.5 d.

- [Design doc](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/Per-chain-airgap-and-DelayedWETH-delay-proposed-changes-and-design-3e5f153ee162809ca7ebc1cf92d1e2ab)

topPRs.title: op-reth: model-based test of the proofs engine state machine
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
A randomized, model-based test of the proofs engine (`rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine`): random interleavings of commits, reorgs, reverts, sync targets, flushes, failed saves, stale notifications and crashes, driven over reth's persistence model, with the store and the engine held to a reference model after every step. The engine's bugs are interleaving bugs (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#464, #477, #478), and the deterministic cases of #23441 and #23449 only cover the interleavings someone thought of.

## What the test does

New integration target `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/tests/engine_model.rs` (its own target so that it and the live target do not share a time budget):

- **Reference model** (`tests/engine_model/model.rs`): the canonical chain as the consensus layer holds it (hash, parent, state root per block), the proof window, a lower bound on what the store has persisted, the fork points whose hash the engine holds for certain, and the engine's possible states as a small set of `(tip, sync target)` candidates. Saves and the sync loop run in the background, so the model predicts a set of outcomes per step and the harness narrows it with the tip it observes once the engine settles. It knows nothing of the engine's internals.
- **Simulated reth**: the existing `SimulatedReth` from `tests/live/simulated_reth.rs` (a real `BlockchainProvider` driven by reth's threshold rule), extended with `revert_to`, `crash_and_restart` (loses everything above reth's persisted tip and reopens from the database) and a `persisted` accessor. Faults: a store wrapper whose next write transaction fails (`tests/engine_model/faults.rs`, for a failed save), and a block reported as replaced through a stale `ChainCommitted` delivered after reth reorged it away (the execute path then finds no parent state).
- **Actions** (`tests/engine_model/actions.rs`), chosen per step with proptest: `Commit{n}`, `Reorg{depth, length}`, `Revert{depth}`, `SyncTo{n}` (reth commits `n` blocks the engine only learns of through a sync target), `Flush`, `FailNextSave`, `StaleCommit{depth, length}`, `BogusReorg` (a one-block reorg on a parent no block has, at a fork point the engine knows), and `Crash(Same)` (drop the engine without flushing, reopen the store, spawn a fresh engine, `sync_to(best)`, then reth rebuilds the lost blocks from the same chain and the harness delivers them as live notifications, with no WAL replay). `Crash(Different)` exists but only the tracked-bug run enables it.
- **Invariants after every step** (`tests/engine_model/invariants.rs`): the engine settles on a tip the model predicts within 30 s; the store's earliest and latest blocks are on the canonical chain; the latest is at or below the engine's tip and at or above what the store had persisted; the window holds at most its configured size; the stored state at the window's ends and at the last fork point serves proofs that hash to the canonical state root there (window and views read in one MDBX read transaction, so a concurrent save cannot prune a height from under the check); every valid delivery is taken (a `ParentHashMismatch` is accepted only where the model says the engine's tip at that height is another block, which a stale notification can cause); a reorg or revert at or below the window's earliest block is refused with `UnwindBeyondEarliest` naming an earliest block the window held around the call, and ends the case since reth moved on without the store; a reorg whose first block does not build on the stored fork block is refused with the stored hash; at the end of a case, after settling, fewer blocks than the persistence threshold stay buffered. Every engine call runs on its own thread with a 30 s bound, so a stalled or panicked engine fails the case instead of hanging it (#23392).
- **Shrinking**: proptest shrinks the action sequence and the configuration; actions are interpreted against the current state (depths clamp to what reth holds in memory), so every sequence is valid. A failure prints the minimal sequence plus the harness transcript of each step (engine tip, store window, reth head), and the first failing case is printed as found, before shrinking, so a run that nextest cuts short still shows it. A tip the model allows on no path fails at once instead of waiting out the settle bound. `ENGINE_MODEL_TRANSCRIPT=1` prints the transcript of passing cases too.
- **Model unit tests** (`model.rs`, `rstest`): the delivery rules (at or below the tip, next block, parent state missing, beyond the next block, mid-sync, refusals on a stale tip), reorg and revert skip-or-unwind, settling, and the restart bounds.

## Matrix

Sampled per case: reth persistence threshold {7, 50} x state masking {0; 30 only with threshold 50, since reth rejects masking + buffer target >= threshold} x memory-block-buffer target {5} x engine (persistence, backpressure) thresholds {(1, 2), (5, 10)} x proofs path by verification interval {0 (index), 1 (execute), 4 (mixed)} x proof window {1000 (never pruned), 4 (pruned on every save)}. Store: `MdbxProofsStorage` in a tempdir. Masking is a parameter of the persistence model only: on develop reth has no partial persistence, so it only decides which persisted blocks stay in memory (see #23441).

Default 24 cases, up to 24 steps each; `PROPTEST_CASES=<n>` raises it (the config goes through `contextualize_config`, so the other `PROPTEST_*` variables apply too). `rust/.config/nextest.toml` gives the `engine_model` binary a 1 m slow period and a 5 m limit, since the whole proptest is one test and a failing case shrinks for up to a minute on top of the run.

## Seams

- `EngineHandle::tip()` under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-utils"))`, next to `flush()`: the model has to wait for the sync loop to settle without side effects, and the only other way to read the tip (probing with a block above it) raises the sync target when the engine is behind.
- `tests/live/chain.rs`: the chain and store helpers of `tests/live.rs`, moved so that both integration targets share them (`tests/live.rs` keeps its scenario runner and tests).
- `SimulatedReth::{persisted, revert_to, crash_and_restart}`, and `reorg_block`, `reorg_block_without_data` and `UNRELATED_PARENT` moved there from `reorg_revert_edges.rs` so both targets share them; `BlockView::read_from(provider, ...)` and `ProofTarget::accounts(...)`.

Left for later, from the `rust-code-reviewer` pass: a shared `DiskSnapshot` in `store_view.rs` (`reorg_revert_edges.rs` has one), one store wrapper with hooks instead of `StoreWithSaveFaults`, `StoreWithWriteGate` and `StoreWithReadHook`, and `Scenario::assert_tip` reading `engine.tip()` instead of probing.

## Local verification

```
cd rust
cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test engine_model
# test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; finished in 14.01s  (the proptest at 24 cases plus the model's unit cases)

cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-trie --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo +nightly-2026-08-22 fmt --all -- --check                                   # clean
```

## Tracked bugs reproduced (ignored, naming the issue)

**ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#464** (store ahead of reth after an unclean shutdown). `engine_and_store_follow_the_model_through_crashes_rebuilding_a_different_chain` is the random run with `Crash(Different)` enabled; it shrinks to the two-step sequence that `store_follows_reth_through_a_crash_rebuilding_a_different_chain` replays deterministically:

```
minimal failing input: config = Config { cadence: (persistence 1, backpressure 2), persistence: threshold 7, verification_interval: 0, window: 1000 },
actions = [Commit { count: 1 }, Crash(Different)]

Error: the store's latest block 1:0x1e41e789dfc0bb9a57adb1b27b9a31fce50bb89feacc13f39c0f3295ee19f307 is not on the canonical chain, whose block 1 is 0x4f527f04ca93da271b1fd73d0e552863b36888b1b9852b5ab312ad8f72a2a20b
--- steps ---
step 0: Commit { count: 1 }
  engine tip 1, store blocks 0..=0, reth head 1
step 1: Crash(Different)
  crash: reth loses blocks 1..=1 and rebuilds them (Different)
  restart: the store serves through block 1, reth's head is 0
```

The harness restarts the ExEx the way it starts today (fresh engine, `sync_to(best)`, live notifications). #23358 adds a startup reconcile to the ExEx; the PR that un-skips these cases has to add the same step to `Harness::crash`.

**ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#478** (`FinishedHeight` acknowledges heights not yet persisted). `sync_loop_completes_while_reth_prunes_bodies_through_the_acknowledged_tip` runs `[SyncTo { count: 40 }, Commit { count: 1 }]` with reth pruning bodies through the acknowledged tip (`Config::body_pruning`):

```
Error: the engine did not settle within 30s: its tip is NumHash { number: 0, hash: 0x37f157e831e926dc33d479b5c3a6fabefdeeffd9e1735075959b45878a66602b }, the model expects one of [NumHash { number: 40, hash: 0x178862dcc49ec13002cb60187c4a81b188b0cd36ac274a5a943cd02323b04ecc }], the store holds blocks 0..=0
--- steps ---
step 0: SyncTo { count: 40 }
  reth pruned bodies through block 32
```

The pruner model is `SimulatedReth::prune_bodies_through` from #23449, called with the notification tip the ExEx acknowledges.

## Findings from the random runs

- The first runs failed on a harness race, not an engine bug: reading the window and the block views in separate read transactions let a save that pruned the window land in between. `BlockView::read_from` reads them from one transaction now.
- A stale `ChainCommitted` whose parent the sync loop has already replaced makes the engine return `ParentHashMismatch` (its tip at that height is the replacing block). That is the engine's contract and the model predicts it; for the ExEx it is fatal (`handle_notification` returns the error). The window is narrow (the loop has to cross the reorg point while the ExEx processes the stale notification) and no issue tracks it yet; it is not reproduced deterministically here.

Stacked on #23449, #23445, #23442, #23441, #23437, #23434, #23429, #23428, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23381

topPRs.title: op-reth: test the proofs engine reorg and revert edges and check unwind targets
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Deterministic tests for the proofs engine's reorg, revert and unwind tasks at the boundaries the model-based test may not reach, with the two engine checks they found missing, and the ExEx executing a reorged chain that carries no trie data instead of failing the node.

The reorg task never checked the first new block's parent against the stored fork block, and nothing refused an unwind at or below the window's earliest block before the store saw it (MDBX refuses it; the in-memory store underflowed at block 0 and otherwise removed the earliest block). `handle_chain_reorged` returned an error for a new chain without trie data, which reth turns into a node exit.

## Changes

- `EngineState::unwind` (shared by the reorg and unwind tasks) now drains any in-flight save, then before touching anything refuses a target at or below `earliest` (`EngineError::Storage(UnwindBeyondEarliest)`) and a target whose parent differs from the stored block below it (`ParentHashMismatch`). The stores keep only the window's end hashes, so the engine buffer retains the hashes of the blocks it persisted (bounded to 1024) to verify forks below the disk tip within a process lifetime. A restarted engine cannot verify a fork below its disk tip; that cell is an `#[ignore]`d test (see below).
- `EngineHandle::reorg` takes `Vec<ReorgBlock>`, each block either `Index { block, hashed_state, trie_updates }` or `Execute(block)`; the task runs each through the same code as `index_block` and `execute_block`, so every block gets the gap and parent checks (an executed block the engine has to skip no longer lets the next indexed one land on a gap). The ExEx picks per block with the rule `ChainCommitted` uses (trie data present and verification not due → index, else execute), shared in `precomputed_trie_data`.
- `PersistenceState::unwind` no longer waits for the in-flight save itself; `EngineState::unwind` drains it first, in one place. The two rejections log at `warn`.
- `InMemoryProofsStorage::unwind_history` follows the trait contract: no-op above `latest`, `UnwindBeyondEarliest` at or below `earliest`, no underflow.
- `ParentHashMismatch`'s docs now describe the unwind case too.

## Tests

Engine live tests in `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/tests/live/reorg_revert_edges.rs`, over backend {InMemory, Mdbx} × flush cadence {(1, 2), (5, 10)} unless noted, each on a seven-block transfer chain. The engine's tip is read through the parent check of a probe block; the persisted history is compared table by table with a fresh store indexed over reth's final canonical chain (`BlockView` / `assert_same_view`), and its proofs are verified against reth's state roots.

| Case | Test | Cells |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | `reorg_replaces_the_stored_blocks_above_the_fork` | × path {Index at fork 6, Execute at fork 3, Mixed at fork 4} |
| (a) | `reorg_not_building_on_the_stored_fork_block_fails_and_changes_nothing` | × fork {6 (buffer or save), 2 (save), 0 (anchor)} × path |
| (a) restart | `restarted_engine_rejects_a_reorg_not_building_on_a_block_below_its_disk_tip` | `#[ignore]`, see Findings |
| (b) | `unwind_or_reorg_at_or_below_the_earliest_block_fails_and_changes_nothing` | × {unwind at earliest, reorg below earliest, reorg at the anchor below a pruned window, unwind at the anchor as earliest} |
| (b) control | `unwind_to_the_block_above_the_earliest_keeps_only_the_earliest` | pruned window |
| (b) in flight | `unwind_at_a_block_the_in_flight_save_prunes_fails_after_the_save` | pruned window; pins that the checks run against the window as the in-flight save leaves it |
| (c) | `revert_of_buffered_blocks_unwinds_the_buffer_and_leaves_the_disk_untouched` | cadence (5, 10) only × revert from {6, 7} |
| (c) in flight | `revert_sent_during_an_in_flight_save_ends_with_the_disk_as_it_was` | |
| (d) | `reorg_sent_during_an_in_flight_save_ends_consistent_with_reth` | × path |

A `StoreWithWriteGate` holds the engine's next write transaction so the save stays in flight until the case releases it. Whether the engine dequeues the revert or reorg before or after the held save completes is not observable from outside (both orders must end the same, and the tests assert that end state); the pruned-window in-flight case is the one where the order changes the outcome, and it pins it. `SimulatedReth` gained `reorg_with(number, specs)`, `executed_block`, `genesis`, `num_hash` and `spawn_engine_with_window`; `FlushCadence` and `Backend` moved to `live.rs` for sharing.

Under cadence (1, 2) no block stays in the buffer outside a save in flight, so (c)'s "(1, 2)" cells are the in-flight revert test.

ExEx tests in `rust/op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs`:
- (e) `chain_reorged_without_trie_data_executes_the_new_chain` × backend: reth's canonical in-memory state holds the new chain, the notification carries no trie data, the store ends on the new tip and `FinishedHeight` acknowledges it.
- (f) `chain_reorged_with_different_fork_blocks_fails_and_changes_nothing`: the error is returned, the store keeps its tip, no event is sent. `handle_chain_reorged`'s docs state the expectation.
- `precomputed_trie_data_follows_the_verification_interval`: a table over interval {0, 2} × block × trie data present/absent.

Unit tests: `engine::buffer::state` (`hash_at` through prune and unwind, bound), `engine::state` (unwind at the anchor, unwind onto a contradicted parent), and `tests/lib.rs` `test_unwind_history_*` over both backends.

## Local verification

All from `rust/` with the shared target dir, on the final commit:

- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test live` — 120 passed, 8 ignored (6 pre-existing `abandoned_fork` cells from #23441 and the 2 restart cells here), 40.0 s wall for the whole live target (21.9 s before this PR).
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test live -- reorg_revert_edges` — 64 passed, 2 ignored, 18.3 s.
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --lib` — 248 passed (28 under `engine::`, including the 5 new buffer and state tests).
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test lib` — 94 passed (8 of them the new `test_unwind_history_*` cells over InMemory and Mdbx).
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p reth-optimism-exex --lib` — 19 passed (12 existing, 2 new reorg tests, 5 `precomputed_trie_data` cases); `cargo test -p reth-optimism-exex --doc --all-features` — 1 passed (the crate doctest needs `--all-features` for `OP_MAINNET`, as `just test-docs` runs it; unchanged by this PR).
- `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-trie -p reth-optimism-exex --all-targets` — zero warnings; `just fmt-check` — clean.

The `rust-code-reviewer` agent ran on the diff; its findings (the reorg task's `Index` arm bypassing `index_block`'s checks, the drain-before-check ordering untested, the in-flight test names, dead code in `PersistenceState::unwind`, naming and dedup) are addressed above.

Every matrix cell of the engine tests ran locally (both backends × both cadences); the only cells not run are the `#[ignore]`d restart cells, which fail by design today.

## Findings

- (a) and (b) fail on develop without the engine checks: with `self.check_unwind_target(to)?` removed from `EngineState::unwind`, all 28 cells of the two tests fail. (a) `reorg_not_building_on_the_stored_fork_block_fails_and_changes_nothing`: all 12 cells panic with `the reorg does not build on the stored fork block: ()`, i.e. `EngineHandle::reorg` returned `Ok(())` and inserted the chain on the wrong parent. (b) `unwind_or_reorg_at_or_below_the_earliest_block_fails_and_changes_nothing`: the 8 Mdbx cells get `got Persistence(Storage(UnwindBeyondEarliest { .. }))`, the store refusing only after the engine drained the save and sent the unwind to the persistence service; with develop's `InMemoryProofsStorage::unwind_history` the 8 InMemory cells panic with `the unwind would remove the window's earliest block: ()`, the unwind returning `Ok(())` after removing the earliest block.
- A restarted engine knows no hash below its store's latest block, so a reorg onto a wrong fork block there is accepted; `restarted_engine_rejects_a_reorg_not_building_on_a_block_below_its_disk_tip` is `#[ignore]`d naming this issue and #23385. Fixing it means keeping every block's hash in the store (a schema change), which is out of this issue's scope.
- The in-memory store's `unwind_history` subtracted one from the target without checking `earliest` or `latest`, so an unwind to block 0 panicked the persistence thread and an unwind above `latest` moved `latest` to a block it never stored.

Stacked on #23442, #23441, #23437, #23434, #23429, #23428, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23391
